lines: THE WORD MARVEL ISN'T ALLOWED TO PUT ON A COVER

segments.text: Marvel almost didn't happen. Its founder was two seats away from dying in 1937.

vis.prompt: Realistic 1930s silver passenger airship in flight over the open ocean at golden hour, elegant Art Deco engineering, twin tail fins, dramatic clouds, documentary matte-painting style, unbranded — no flags, no insignia, no national markings, no text anywhere on the hull

segments.text: Martin Goodman's fresh off his honeymoon in Europe. Wants to come home in style — a seat on the Hindenburg. First class. Peak nineteen-thirties luxury.

vis.prompt: Realistic 1930s transatlantic travel agency interior: an ornate wooden booking counter, frosted glass partitions, a brass desk lamp, an ink pen and blotter, a rack of unlabeled travel brochures, stacked leather luggage in the foreground, tall arched windows with warm golden-hour light, documentary matte-painting style, elegant atmosphere, no signage, no departures board, no readable text of any kind, no faces, empty of people

segments.text: But he waits too long. Only two tickets left, and they're not together — three days apart from his own wife, crossing the Atlantic. No thanks.

vis.prompt: Realistic close-up of a 1930s leather-bound passenger booking ledger open on a wooden desk, a clerk's hand pointing at two circled seat numbers scattered non-adjacently across a hand-drawn airship deck-plan diagram, a rubber stamp and brass inkwell nearby, warm desk-lamp lighting, documentary matte-painting style, muted sepia-gold palette, no readable text beyond generic marks, no faces

segments.text: So he books a plane instead. No big decision. Barely a footnote at the time.

vis.prompt: Realistic 1930s twin-propeller passenger airplane parked on a tarmac at dusk, boarding stairs down, a suitcase and travel trunk in the foreground, golden hour lighting, documentary matte-painting style, no visible airline branding or text, no faces

segments.text: May sixth, nineteen thirty-seven. The Hindenburg goes up in flames while landing in New Jersey. Thirty-six people don't walk away.
Two years later, Goodman starts a tiny publishing company. Needs cheap help. Hires his wife's seventeen-year-old cousin.

vis.prompt: Realistic 1930s New York publishing office interior: a cluttered wooden desk with a manual typewriter, stacks of blank pulp-paper proofs, a rotary telephone, a coat rack by the door, warm desk-lamp lighting through venetian blinds casting striped shadows, documentary matte-painting style, no visible readable text or logos, no faces, empty of people

segments.text: That cousin's name was Stanley Lieber. You know him as Stan Lee. One sold-out airship, and there's no Marvel at all.
